subject: Recap & asks: context footprint, token mix, and target $/1M for Avery Labs pilot
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@averylabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & asks: context footprint, token mix, and target $/1M for Avery Labs pilot

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size a pricing proposal that matches your usage profile.

Key takeaways from the call (what you confirmed):
- Primary use case: multi-turn product Q&A + short generation for marketing snippets (high variance in output length).
- Approx current weekly volume: ~8–9M tokens (expected ramp to ~30–40M tokens/month if pilot proves out).
- Average prompt tokens (from your sampling): ~180–240 tokens.
- Average completion tokens: ~600–900 tokens, with a long-tail of larger outputs.
- Context length needs (by request share): ~70% will fit comfortably in 8k windows, ~25% require 32k, and ~5% may benefit from >32k / 128k when we include entire conversation history + attachments.

For pricing, you mentioned an internal target of roughly $750 per 1M tokens as a goal (assuming predictable performance and some discounts for commit). We want to confirm a few details so our quote is aligned:

A. Confirm token mix and monthly run-rate
- Can you confirm the expected average monthly token consumption for the 12-week pilot window? You mentioned a conservative estimate of 30M tokens/month and an upside to 45M/month. If you provide a one-number guidance (conservative / expected), we’ll model both.

B. Confirm context-size distribution by percent (8k / 32k / 128k)
- We used the split above (70/25/5). Please correct if off. This materially affects model selection and unit cost.

C. Target $/1M tokens and procurement preference
- You said ~$750/1M as a target. Is that net-effective (post any internal marketplace fees) or list price you expect us to hit for the pilot? Also confirm if you prefer a Hosted (pay-as-you-go) pilot or a short Dedicated-reserved pilot (we can offer better $/1M with a short commit).

D. Success criteria & next steps
- Proposed pilot: 30-day functional pilot, automatic tracing enabled, token-level cost dashboards, and one eval set to measure quality regressions.
- If we agree on price and scope, we’ll send a short SOW + MSA and a billing/PO worksheet.

Attachments: Avery_pilot_estimate.xlsx (simple token-volume worksheets) and mutual_action_plan.pdf (proposed milestones).

Would you be able to confirm A–C by end of day Monday? Once we have that we’ll produce three pricing scenarios (hosted PAYG, 3-month reserved, and 6-month committed Dedicated) with modeled unit economics, estimated GPU footprint, and an ROI sketch.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@averylabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Labs Procurement <procurement@averylabs.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & asks: context footprint, token mix, and target $/1M for Avery Labs pilot

Mina — thanks for the clear recap, that matches how we saw the call. A few clarifications to lock down the numbers: 

1) Monthly run-rate for pilot window: please model the conservative scenario at 30M tokens/month and the expected at 40M tokens/month. If the pilot hits success criteria we expect to scale to ~60M tokens/month within 3 months.

2) Token averages from our telemetry (post-call sample):
- avg prompt tokens: 200 (we batch some metadata in prompts)
- avg completion tokens: 720 (median ~480, mean pulled up by long-tail)
- distribution on context size: ~72% 8k, ~23% 32k, ~5% 128k/very-long. The 128k bucket is rare but important for certain enterprise threads (legal/contract review flows).

3) Target price: $750/1M tokens is our internal target after discounts. We understand this may require a commit; we are open to a short reserved pilot (30–90 days) if you can demonstrate a path to ~$700–750 effective with a 3–6 month commit. Also flagging procurement: we require a short SOW and a PO for pilot spend >$25k.

4) A couple of asks for your pricing model: please break out per-1M token pricing by window size (8k vs 32k vs 128k) and show the impact of prefix caching and KV cache reuse on effective token consumption (we have many repeated prefixes across sessions).

I’ll loop in procurement once you have a ballpark estimate and SOW.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of ML Platform, Avery Labs
samir@averylabs.com | +1 (617) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@averylabs.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing scenarios & token economics (draft)

Samir — per Mina’s note and your clarifications, I attached a short set of pricing scenarios (dedicated_pricing_options.pdf) and summarized the unit economics below so you can see how we modeled the $/1M targets.

Modeled inputs (from your numbers):
- avg prompt tokens: 200
- avg completion tokens: 720
- token mix used for modeling: 72% 8k / 23% 32k / 5% 128k
- conservative monthly tokens: 30M | expected: 40M

Quick unit-econ summary (effective $/1M tokens):
- Hosted PAYG (no commit): 8k tier = $1,000/1M | 32k tier = $1,450/1M | 128k class = $2,700/1M
- Dedicated, 3-month reserved (30M/mo commit): 8k effective = $720/1M | 32k = $1,100/1M | 128k = $2,000/1M
- Dedicated, 6-month reserved (30M/mo commit): 8k effective = $650/1M | 32k = $1,000/1M | 128k = $1,800/1M

Notes on assumptions and levers we used:
- Caching & batching: we model ~12% effective token reduction from prefix caching and batch KV reuse on your workload (you mentioned repeated prompt templates).
- Quantization & model variant: additional 8–12% cost delta if you are comfortable with an int8-quantized variant for lower-cost paths; we can A/B quality on a subset of traffic.
- SLO & fallback: Dedicated includes automatic routing to a smaller-capacity host under heavy load; we modeled fallback cost at hosted PAYG rates for overflow.

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm the conservative/expected monthly token numbers (30M / 40M).
2) We prepare a 30-day SOW and a short billing worksheet for Procurement (if >$25k we’ll need a PO).
3) If you want preferred economics closer to $700–750/1M for the 8k bucket, we can produce a 6-month commit proposal with a phased ramp and a performance-based credit if latency or availability targets are missed.

I’ve attached dedicated_pricing_options.pdf with the full tables and model-level recommendations. Mina — I left anchors for the SOW timeline and acceptance criteria.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0138

From: Samir Patel <samir@averylabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Avery Labs Procurement <procurement@averylabs.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing scenarios & token economics (draft)

Thanks Marissa & Mina — this is helpful and exactly the detail we need. Procurement: we’re good to proceed with a 30-day pilot target kicking off in early July. Mina, please send the SOW + short MSA and a pilot PO template (we’ll route internally). We’ll start with the 6-month committed economics as the target to negotiate toward (aiming for ~650–750/1M on the 8k effective bucket).

Samir
--
Samir Patel
Head of ML Platform, Avery Labs
samir@averylabs.com
